title: Uluzzian technocomplex (Grotta del Cavallo, Italy)
summary: The Uluzzian is a stone-tool technocomplex of southern Italy. At Grotta del Cavallo its start is placed about 45,000 calendar years ago. A reanalysis of two child molars from the cave attributed them to anatomically modern humans, and its authors concluded the makers were not Neanderthals; a 2015 study disputes this and finds Neanderthal authorship the parsimonious reading.

uncertainty.note: Start is Zilhão et al.: Uluzzian start ca. 45,000 calendar years ago (year = 1950 minus 45,000 = -43050). Benazzi et al. date the teeth to 45,000-43,000 cal BP, giving the plus range. The end of the technocomplex is not stated in an opened source, so the record is dated to its start only.

as_recorded.value: teeth "must date to ∼45,000–43,000 calendar years before present"

where.modern_name: Grotta del Cavallo, Santa Caterina, Nardò, Lecce province, Apulia, Italy
where.historical_name: Grotta del Cavallo, near the Bay of Uluzzo, southern Italy; no polity at this date

importance.justification: An early Upper Palaeolithic industry in southern Italy whose makers, Neanderthals or modern humans, are still debated.
